title: Distributed Memory Architectures
summary: Distribute model weights, activations, and attention state across devices with an explicit communication and failure model.
overview: Distributed memory architectures in model infrastructure address the memory required to execute a model across multiple accelerators or memory tiers. Tensor parallelism partitions tensor computation, pipeline parallelism partitions layers, and other schemes distribute experts or separate prefill from decoding. This topic concerns model execution memory, distinct from an agent’s durable conversational memory.

Memory does not become a free shared pool. Partitioning introduces communication, synchronization, topology constraints, and coordinated failure. CPU offload or remote cache transfer trades scarce accelerator memory for bandwidth and latency. Choose a strategy after estimating weights, activations, key-value cache, and runtime overhead for the target context and concurrency.

production.poc: A prototype inventories memory components and tests whether quantization or smaller batches can meet the requirement on one device.
production.production: Production selects a supported partitioning strategy, benchmarks communication, and treats distributed workers as a coordinated serving group.
production.scale: Enterprise scale plans topology-aware placement, failure domains, cache movement, and capacity accounting across heterogeneous nodes and workloads.

useCase.title: Serving a large technical-analysis model
useCase.situation: A research platform needs a model and context configuration that exceed one accelerator’s usable memory.
useCase.problem: Naive CPU offload fits the weights but makes interactive analysis too slow.
useCase.requirement: Select a supported multi-device layout that meets both capacity and latency requirements.
useCase.architecture: The team profiles weights and cache, then benchmarks partitioned serving on a high-bandwidth worker group.
runtime: A request is admitted only when the whole serving group is ready.
Telemetry separates communication time from model compute and tracks cache growth with context length.
useCase.failure: If one worker fails, the group stops accepting requests and incomplete generations restart under an explicit client policy.
useCase.impact: Measure per-request latency, accepted throughput, memory headroom, and communication fraction; adding devices can increase cost without improving latency.

tradeoffs.benefit: Distributes large tensor operations and weight memory.
tradeoffs.cost: Requires frequent communication and compatible partition dimensions.

tradeoffs.benefit: Distributes layers across devices or nodes.
tradeoffs.cost: Can introduce pipeline bubbles and stage imbalance.

tradeoffs.benefit: Extends effective capacity beyond accelerator memory.
tradeoffs.cost: Adds transfer latency and bandwidth pressure.

failures.detection: Communication spans exceed useful compute time.
failures.recovery: Change placement, parallel degree, or model configuration.

failures.detection: The distributed request can no longer continue consistently.
failures.recovery: Fail the affected generation and recover the coordinated group.

mistakes.mistake: Confusing model memory with agent memory
mistakes.fix: Separate inference partitioning from durable workflow state.
Include KV cache, activations, and runtime overhead.

mistakes.mistake: Assuming more devices always improve speed
mistakes.fix: Benchmark topology and communication under real concurrency.

whenToUse: Use when a validated model configuration exceeds one device.
Use when supported parallelism improves measured capacity or throughput.
Use with adequate communication infrastructure and operational expertise.
whenNotToUse: Avoid distribution when one device meets the objective more simply.
Do not assume arbitrary devices form efficient shared memory.
checklist: Compare cost and latency against simpler alternatives.
